parts:
First of all, thanks for reading! Any suggestions are super welcome!

After successfully installed PyStan on my local desktop (Ubuntu), I am trying to install PyStan on the Cluster, then I got some trouble.

Procedure:
1st, install Cython.
My username on the cluster is jeffdu.
Install Cython on local directory:
down the Cython tar from http://cython.org/release/Cython-0.23.4.tar.gz
gunzip, and change to Chthon directory:
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/home/jeffdu/lib64/python2.6/site-packages/
Then 
python setup.py install --prefix=/home/jeffdu

Everything worked well.

2nd, install NumPy
Basically the same as step 1. 

3rd, install PyStan
wget https://pypi.python.org/packages/source/p/pystan/pystan-2.8.0.2.tar.gz

tar zxvf pystan-2.8.0.2.tar.gz
cd pystan-2.8.0.2
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/home/jeffdu/lib64/python2.6/site-packages/
python setup.py install --prefix=/home/jeffdu

Then, I got some errors during installing:

parts:
hi


I also work on a cluster with Python 26, but it's a good practice not to work with a system Python rather in a virtual environment (so that e.g.  upgrades to system don't affect your project)


In my experience, installing Continuum's Anaconda distribution (it's free) is the easiest route. You can install to home folder, source the environment and pip install pystan (which will handle dependencies if any aren't in Anaconda distribution). If you have space quota, try the miniconda installer, where you only install what's necessary. 


hope this helps,

marmaduke

can get Python 2.7 installed or enabled. PyStan doesn't work under
